title: 機械学習システムとテスト (2/4) (Japanese only)
reason: Japanese-language Citadel AI blog (part 2 of a 4-part series on testing ML pipelines); body is entirely Japanese with no English version at this URL, so it is a §1 hard drop before any finding test is reached.

title: Auditing vs Assurance: What's the Difference?
rule_cited: §2 tests 1 and 2 — definitional explainer, no evaluator-asserted evidence-backed claim
reason: Holistic AI explainer defining 'audit' vs 'assurance' and listing the five lifecycle stages an audit can examine; no system was tested and no measured result, observed behaviour or process fact is reported.

title: Introducing the ML Model Attribution Challenge
reason: Call for contestants for the ML Model Attribution Challenge (runs 12 Aug–9 Sep 2022, prizes up to USD $10,000); it announces a competition that had not yet run, so there is no measured result to code.

title: Assessing the Impact of Algorithmic Systems
rule_cited: §2 tests 1 and 2 — explainer on AIAs/DPIAs and pending legislation, no evidence-backed claim
reason: Holistic AI explainer distinguishing Algorithmic Impact Assessments from Data Protection Impact Assessments and summarising the EU AI Act, US Algorithmic Accountability Act and California WTAA; nothing is evaluated.

title: Introducing ML:Integrity
rule_cited: §2 — event announcement plus opinion; opinions and plans are not findings
reason: Robust Intelligence CEO's announcement of the October ML:Integrity conference plus a conceptual argument that 'AI risk = (likelihood of an error) x (its potential effect)'; the only quantitative claim (70% of enterprises) is attributed to a Gartner report, failing §2 test 1.

title: NIST's AI Risk Management Framework Explained
rule_cited: §2 test 1 — summary of someone else's work (NIST's draft AI RMF)
reason: Holistic AI explainer walking through the Govern/Map/Measure/Manage core of NIST's second-draft AI RMF; every substantive claim is NIST's, not Holistic AI's, and no system was assessed.

title: Supporting the Royal Australian Navy's Campaign Plan for Robotics and Autonomous Systems: Enhancing Innovation
rule_cited: §2 test 2 — recommendations and approaches, not evidence-backed evaluation findings
reason: RAND Australia advisory study for the Royal Australian Navy on innovation and rapid-acquisition practices for robotics/autonomous systems and AI; its 'Key Takeaways' and 'Recommendations' are prescriptive acquisition-process advice, and no AI model or system was evaluated.

title: Facial Recognition is a Controversial and High-Risk Technology. Algorithmic Risk Management Can Help
rule_cited: §2 test 1 — comparator/third-party results cited in passing, not asserted by the evaluator
reason: Holistic AI commentary on facial recognition risk; every empirical claim (Gender Shades, NIST's 189-algorithm investigation, the Detroit and Met police failure rates) is someone else's result cited in passing, and the rest is risk-management advice.

title: How Hired Chose Holistic AI to be Their Auditing Partner
rule_cited: §2 — partnership news contains no findings; results are forward-looking
reason: Holistic AI post on being selected as Hired's bias-audit partner; it states the audit examined explainability, bias and privacy but reports no result, saying only that 'the results of this audit will soon be made public', so nothing is evidence-backed here (§2 test 2).

title: Why Do We Need AI Auditing and Assurance?
rule_cited: §2 test 1 — recounts third-party investigations, not the evaluator's own work
reason: Holistic AI post arguing the need for AI auditing by recounting the ProPublica COMPAS investigation, Amazon's scrapped resume tool and the Apple Card credit-limit controversy; all three are other parties' findings summarised here.

title: New York City Bias Audit Law: Here's Everything You Need to Know
rule_cited: §2 tests 1 and 2 — regulatory explainer summarising DCWP's proposed amendments
reason: Holistic AI explainer on NYC Local Law 144 and the DCWP's 19 September 2022 proposed amendments (independent-auditor definition, selection rate and impact ratio requirements); it reports regulation, not an evaluation.

title: Process evaluation of the Multi-Agency Advisory Service (MAAS) for AI and data-driven technologies in health and social care
rule_cited: §2 test 2 — project page describing work in progress, no results reported
reason: RAND Europe project page for a commissioned process evaluation of the MAAS advisory service; it lists the evaluation's objectives and methods and states future work ('We will also interview developers...'), reporting no results, and MAAS is a regulatory advisory service rather than an AI model.

title: How to Manage the Risk of AI Bias in Identity Verification
rule_cited: §2 test 2 — conceptual explainer and service pitch, no measured result
reason: Holistic AI/Braithwate explainer on how identity-verification ML works and how unrepresentative training data can produce differential false-rejection and false-acceptance rates; the claims are generic mechanism description and advice, with no IDV system tested.

title: Moving in the Right Direction: AI Bill of Rights
rule_cited: §2 — opinion piece; opinions and forward-looking commentary are not findings
reason: Robust Intelligence policy commentary on the White House Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights, quoting its five principles and arguing it is non-binding and under-covers education and law enforcement; this is opinion about policy, not an evaluation.
